Ever remembered as the founder of the well-known centre of learning, the Banāras Hindu University (BHU), Paṇḍit Madanmohan Māḷavīya was born in A.

at Allahabad in Uttar Pradesh (then known as the United Provinces). He was the son of Brajnāth, who was himself a great scholar and author in Sanskrit.
Madanmohan MāḷavīyaAfter some एदुचतिओन् in traditional Sanskrit learning, he studied in English schools and colleges ultimately getting a degree in law. He worked as a teacher first and later practised law.
Like many of his contemporaries, he too jumped into the freedom movement. He was the president of the Indian National Congress, four times—in 1909, 1918, 1932 and 1933.
Māḷavīya was a devout Hindu and was also a great scholar. He was a powerful speaker in Hindi. He helped in starting and running some important journals.
He was also closely associated with the Hindu Mahāsabhā, an organisation started in 1915 to protect the interests of the Hindus.
